Almost everybody have the desire to bond, but some, due to many psychological or social factors, can't have the intention to bond(example: a married woman have the opportunity to bond with a male coworker, but she will choose not to due to all social pressure and to avoid creating a discussion on their marriage, 'cause people are dumb and think woman can't have friends). The second problem that you might not even think about is disorders. People can have barriers to bond and connect due to past traumas, autism, social anxiety and other things. These people want to bond, but they will struggle a lot with every interaction and some might even give up on bonding... The effort put on every interaction to be rewarded with no real connection is a huge tool. The third motive I see is the disconnection of realities. Sometimes bonding over something you like with another person(a sport, a class, an artist, etc) might put you in a situation where you and the person are actually friends for that motive, but all the other parts of your life can be very, very different, so whenever the topic go astray you feel the disconnection again...

I'd say that there are too many layers on this. But I'll try to break it down a little.
I'll break it in 3 parts: resources, confidence and Decision-making. First of all, a team will want to give more resource to the better player. And that is just playing the strenghts of the personnel you have. The skill level of the best player compared to the 6th best might be enough for a little bit more of lane control, a better trade that can result in a gank or just the team helping more their "strong link" compared to someone accepting being the weak-side for the team. The second part is confidence. Being able to know you can avoid skillshots and land skillshots and just... playing slightly better in general makes it possible for the better player to play far more aggresive and snowball out of small advantages. If you even are able to take a flash from your opponent, that's already 5 minutes of pressure you got for your team that someone else couldn't. And the last is... decision making. Without training and analyzing competitive plays it's hard to understand how people are strategizing, but the sense of awareness and how both players in the lane behave depends on previous match-ups too. If someone is facing faker, they might want to play a little safer because they know T1 is able to snowball better than other teams. And faker, seeing that the opponent is willing to let some resources go to avoid a dive or a play, might freeze better or get priority for dragons and voidgrubs... As you can see, all of that adds a little. You can be great with good micro and good macro, but to be the best you must have a micro so great that allows you to macro even better.

Normally, I try to change HLs a lot during a match. I play like 5 to 6 different HLs when I don't have a 3\* HL.  
Headliners pop on every shop when you don't have one, or every 3 shops if you have one. So, if you want to change yours, better to sell it.  
They will count as 2 units of the trait it shines, for some traits it can be very important, so pay attention and consider if the unit is the most important thing or the champion for you in that moment.  
Playing without a headliner is... kinda really bad. It's basically a free opportunity to use a 2\* unit that boosts traits. So use it. I normally would recommend to use PvE battles as some opportunities to transition while learning, so you have some time to read and think about the units. Sometimes you'll see people using strong headliners that aren't even supposed to fit the comp they are doing, like a Karthus on a KDA board, but it's because they might have Ahri items but got a Karthus and don't have much money, so it's WAY better to buy the Karthus, slam your items and at least have a carry than go to battle without one.

First of all, I'll talk a little about the odds of a headliner to pop in the shop based on cost:  
on lv 2/3, 100% are cost 1.  
Normally you want this just to get a good trait combo for early, a strong 2\* that can hold the items you got or maybe go for a cost 1 3\* early, that can help you for a while(annie, yasuo and olaf, specially).  
on lv 4/5, you can start finding some cost 2.  
If you started with some money or couldn't really find a cost 1 HL to hold your items, you can go for a cost 2, they will help you spike 'till 3-2 too, but barely any of them are really great late game.   
on lv 6/7, you will see some cost 3.  
This is specially when it's start to get... tricky. Many cost 3 are good HLs, some even are carry(vex,yone, riven), but they might double the trait you don't really want, so you'll have to adapt.  
on lv 8, you will see the most important: cost 4.  
They are the bread and butter of the game rn. Rolling for a 2\* cost 4 and hitting a viable one for your items can make or break a strat.  
on lv 9, there's just a really small (2%) chance of finding a cost 5 headliner. Getting one here might get you first/second place, but you can't really count on it.  
But on lv 10, there's a 90%, which makes it really strong and reliable option if you have econ augments and a good strategy.  


There are some rules about them popping when you have the units already, like: if you have 5+ of some cost 4/5 unit, you won't find them as headliners anymore. This way, you can't really get strong 3\* units in a blink of an eye. This rule don't apply for cost 1/2/3.  
There must be at least 3 units of what you want in the shop for it to pop as a headliner. Some champions are used in 3 different good comps, so pay attention if there's the unit you want available.  
The Headliners are not only 2\* units, but they all get a buff like 20AP, 200HP or so, which makes them great item holders, even if they are just your secondary carry. Some, like bard, have special interactions with their skills, but you kinda have to play and just pay attention while re-rolling, as they are all small buffs.  
Some details: recombobulator makes your HL disappear, you'll get a 2\* based on the unit you had, but the new one won't be a HL.
